back2basics.concept: Election Commission of India and electoral process
back2basics.text: The Election Commission of India is a constitutional authority responsible for administering elections to ensure they are free, fair, and transparent. It consists of a Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners who make decisions collectively, usually by majority. The voter list revision process updates the electoral rolls to include eligible voters and remove ineligible ones, which must be done transparently to protect voting rights.

back2basics.concept: Banking Regulation Act and RBI's supervisory role
back2basics.text: The Banking Regulation Act, 1949 empowers the Reserve Bank of India to regulate and supervise banking institutions, including cooperative banks, to ensure their sound functioning and protect depositors. Sections 35A and 56 allow RBI to issue directions to banks in public interest, including restrictions or operational controls, to maintain financial stability and confidence in the banking system.

body.label: Campaign overview
body.text: Launched under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, it aims to reduce drug abuse through preventive education, awareness, treatment, and rehabilitation.

body.text: The campaign has reached over 35.70 crore people, including 14.26 crore youth and 11.24 crore women, with more than 39.91 lakh persons treated and rehabilitated through over 755 de-addiction centres.

body.label: Campaign purpose
body.text: Launched on November 27, 2024, by the Ministry of Women and Child Development, it aims to prevent child marriage through legal enforcement, public awareness, and community participation.

body.label: Legal framework
body.text: The campaign operates under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, which prohibits child marriage, defines penalties, and empowers Child Marriage Prohibition Officers (CMPOs) for prevention and enforcement.

body.label: Campaign achievements
body.text: By November 2026, 6.85 lakh awareness programmes were conducted, reaching 12.47 crore participants, with 42.01 lakh pledges registered and 4,536 child marriage incidents reported on the campaign portal.

body.label: Prevalence decline
body.text: Child marriage prevalence among women aged 20-24 declined from 23.3% in NFHS-5 (2019-21) to 20.1% in NFHS-6 (2023-24), showing progress but uneven across states.

sections.heading: What is the ‘Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat’ campaign?

body.label: Digital platforms
body.text: The ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva’ quiz is accessible via the MY Bharat portal, while the Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat campaign uses a dedicated portal for reporting, awareness tracking, and pledge registration.

body.label: Community engagement
body.text: Both campaigns mobilise citizens, especially youth, through pledges, quizzes, awareness programmes, and involvement of local institutions and public representatives.

body.label: Monitoring and enforcement
body.text: The Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat portal provides data on CMPOs, incident reporting, and awareness activities, enabling evidence-based monitoring and timely preventive action.

back2basics.concept: Foreign Direct Investment and NBFC Credit
back2basics.text: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) involves investment from foreign entities into Indian companies or entities, either through equity or debt, impacting India's external financial position. Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) provide credit to various sectors of the economy and their credit deployment patterns influence economic growth and financial stability.

2026-11-07-am-fe3a07fc97.deck: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) published the provisional results of the 2025-26 Census on Foreign Liabilities and Assets of Indian direct investment entities and the sectoral deployment of credit by Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) as of September 2026. These data provide insights into India's external investment positions and credit flow patterns, relevant for understanding economic growth, financial stability, and policy formulation.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about RBI's 2025-26 Census on Foreign Liabilities and Assets and NBFC credit deployment:
1. Around 97% of Indian entities reporting FDI and/or ODI were unlisted as of end-March 2026.
2. NBFC credit to the industry sector grew faster than credit to agriculture in September 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.trap: Statement 2 is incorrect because NBFC credit to agriculture grew by 17.8% while credit to industry declined to 7.4% in September 2026.

body.label: Scope of census
body.text: The census covers cross-border liabilities and assets of Indian entities including companies, LLPs, AIFs, and partnership firms with inward or outward direct investment.

body.label: Entities reporting FDI and ODI
body.text: A total of 43,123 entities reported foreign direct investment (FDI) and/or overseas direct investment (ODI) as of end-March 2026, with about 97% being unlisted entities holding the major share of FDI equity capital.

body.label: Equity and debt composition
body.text: Non-financial companies accounted for over 90% of FDI equity at face value, and unlisted companies held 96.6% of FDI debt as of March 2026.

body.label: Inward vs outward investment ratio
body.text: The ratio of inward FDI to ODI moderated to 4.2 times by end-March 2026 from 5.5 times a year earlier.

body.label: Top countries for FDI and ODI
body.text: The United States, Mauritius, Singapore, and the United Kingdom were the top sources of inward FDI, while Singapore, the UAE, and the United States were the main destinations for ODI.

body.label: Sectoral distribution
body.text: Manufacturing accounted for the highest share (50.1%) of total outstanding FDI equity capital by market value, followed by services sector with 45%.

sections.heading: What does the RBI Census on Foreign Liabilities and Assets reveal?

body.label: Overall credit growth
body.text: NBFC credit grew by 15.4% year-on-year in September 2026, up from 13.3% a year ago.

body.label: Agriculture credit growth
body.text: Credit to agriculture and allied activities recorded a strong growth of 17.8% compared to 5.2% a year earlier.

body.label: Industry sector credit
body.text: Credit growth in the industry sector declined to 7.4% year-on-year, with subdued growth in infrastructure.

body.label: Services sector credit
body.text: Credit growth in services moderated to 17.3% from 23.0% a year ago, with commercial real estate, trade, and transport operators seeing higher credit growth.

body.label: Retail loans growth
body.text: Retail loans grew at 21.9% year-on-year, with accelerated growth in housing loans, loans against gold jewellery, and vehicle loans.
